concept.name: Descending channel
concept.definition: A channel whose two parallel boundary lines slope downward, enclosing a downtrend's lower highs and lower lows. The upper (resistance) line connects falling highs and the parallel lower (support) line floors the declines; classically read as trend-consistent structure until broken.
concept.intuition: A downtrend with guardrails: each bounce dies at the upper rail, each drop finds footing near the lower rail.
concept.mechanics: Constructed by drawing a down trendline through two or more falling swing highs and a parallel line through the intervening swing low(s). Heuristics sell rallies near the upper rail and cover near the lower; a break above the upper rail warns of trend change.
concept.failure_modes: Downside breaks of the lower rail can be capitulation spikes that immediately reverse; upside breaks catch shorts who assumed the rails would hold.
concept.misconceptions: That a descending channel is purely bearish; an upside break of its resistance rail is a recognized reversal warning.
concept.example: A stock's bounces stall on a falling line through 100, 95, 90 while declines bottom on the parallel line through 92, 87, 82 — a descending channel.
